allowlist.reason: The share outbox still HOLDS obligations (same-owner deliver-give, leftover pull-blob rows); what retired with copy-as-share in #825 is the surface that listed them for a human. Deleting the read would take the outbox's only inspection point with it, so it is held for the #825 dead-give sweep that decides the outbox's shape as a whole.

Edit fulfillment's routing answer (#825, ruling G-edit). Its production seam is the vault gateway's single write door (packages/vault/src/gateway/gateway.ts invoke, beside commonsGrantForCommand), and wiring it there is #825's Docs-integration wave, not the gateway wave: the router returns a route (with refusals such as 'shared for view only') whenever ANY grant exists over a container, so raw wiring today would refuse the OWNER's own edits to subjects they shared for view. The wiring needs actor-awareness plus an end-to-end edit proof, which is exactly what that wave builds; the grant plane's HTTP surface deliberately does not duplicate that door in the meantime.
